steps.speaker: Evelleon
steps.content: Since you won't hear me out, do keep yourself safe when you go back. Don't die too soon.

steps.speaker: Evelleon
steps.content: I'd still like to see you two reunited. Dearest siblings, together at last...

When you open your eyes again, you are in a hospital room. The arrangement is unfamiliar; this is not the Bureau, you realize. Then your gaze finds the emblem on the wall—it's the Ring Research Institute.
At your bedside, Summer stands with her hands planted on her hips, talking animatedly into her phone.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: The hell happened to Chief?! That big dummy got into that much trouble?!

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Relaaax, we got Chief back, safe and sound! We've got two big shots on the case, y'know!

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Especially a certain blonde grump. She did all the heavy lifting. If only she wasn't too shy to show up here.
Seems like she isn't aware you're awake. She's still chattering away into her terminal, giggling and boasting with unmistakable delight. It's Schorl who takes notice first.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Hello, Chief. You're looking better than anticipated. Shall I let everyone know?
You shake your head and simply raise a hand toward it, fingers forming the number seven.

You think back to the moment you were taken. The enemy's original target, Lemma, was right beside you back then. Whatever else she may be, she is still a child. You can't help but wonder how she's faring now.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: If her well-being concerns you so, would you like to go check on her?
[Scene Change]

She's not in the dormitory, nor the lab. You've heard that Lemma pulls more overtime than anyone. She has practically turned her office into a private living space, one she never lets anyone enter. Alright, then. You'll slip over and find out for yourself.

Another long, curving corridor stretches ahead. The entire length is lined with cameras and monitors, which Summer disables with a simple wave of her hand, one after another. That said, what's truly surprising is that Lemma hasn't noticed a thing.

At the corridor's end, a plain, modest door hangs slightly ajar. Through the gap, you can just make out Lemma's voice. She's talking to someone on the phone. She hasn't even realized the door is open, or that someone has arrived. Her spirits have sunk so low that even her voice has gone soft, diminished.

steps.speaker: Lemma
steps.content: Mm... yeah... I do understand. I'm being rational about this. It just... doesn't sit well with me.

steps.speaker: Gentle Voice
steps.content: You contributed so much. Plus, you made an unexpected breakthrough with your dimensional calculations, no?
That voice... you know it from somewhere.

steps.speaker: Lemma
steps.content: But he still got hurt because of my call, at least in part... It was my first time out in the field, seeing it firsthand... Watching someone get injured... it's somehow worse than studying Corruptors...
steps.female_content: But she still got hurt because of my call, at least in part... It was my first time out in the field, seeing it firsthand... Watching someone get injured... it's somehow worse than studying Corruptors...

steps.speaker: Gentle Voice
steps.content: Then go tell him how you feel. Say you were worried. Thank him. If you feel sorry, apologize. Though I'm quite certain he wouldn't mind it at all.
steps.female_content: Then go and tell her how you feel. Say you were worried. Thank her. If you feel sorry, apologize. Though I'm quite certain she wouldn't mind it at all.

steps.speaker: Gentle Voice
steps.content: Think of Keylan and his expedition team. Not all of them were brilliant scientists, yet they still became true companions bound by the same vision. You've always wanted comrades like that, right?

steps.speaker: Lemma
steps.content: ...Yeah.

steps.speaker: Gentle Voice
steps.content: There you go. And look, seems they've already come looking for you.

steps.speaker: Gentle Voice
steps.content: Keep it up, Lemma. You'll do just fine.
And of course, the door gives a long, mournful creak right at this moment of all times. Lemma spins around, and the second she sees you standing there, her face floods with bright red.

steps.speaker: Lemma
steps.content: You—I—wh-who said you could just come in—?!

BAM! Summer catapults herself from behind you, flinging the door wide and tumbling into the room in a maneuver that tears a horrified shriek from Lemma. And at last, you are granted full view of the astonishing chamber belonging to none other than the Ring Research Institute's Chief Researcher, Head of the Observation Hub, genius scientist, and EDGE-07 seat holder among humanity's foremost leaders.

The first thing to seize your attention is an enormous Keylan poster mounted on the wall. Against it stands a glass display case: on its highest shelf, figures of the expedition team; on its bottom, rows of manuscripts, all carefully arranged. You struggle to contain your astonishment as your eyes sweep further across the room. Off to one side, a desk lies strewn with keychains, card sleeves, protective covers, glittering stickers, and expedition team cards—some still only half-finished.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Lemma's idols, so to speak. A rather... extensive collection.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Told you she's one of us! Same old Lemma... What's the point of hiding it?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: So, what'll it be, princess? In the market for the latest collector's edition expedition figures? I'm sure I could coax Faye over at the MBCC Supply Office into helping us develop them.

steps.speaker: Barrie
steps.content: It's totally fine, Lemma. We all look up to idols. It's how we grow, how we feel love. There's nothing to be embarrassed about.

steps.speaker: Enya
steps.content: Exactly! We're into real people, which is way more sophisticated than whatever anime fantasy Summer lives in. We're warriors of real love, comrades on the same front!

steps.speaker: Sarah
steps.content: Your idol's figure is a little faded. Honestly, it kind of looks like he's balding. Do you want me to touch it up?
The blonde girl's cheeks burn brighter and brighter, the tension coiling so tight a single pinprick might undo her, and that's when her gaze finds yours.

You meet her eyes, a dozen unspoken questions crowding your mind. Was she hurt? Was she frightened? How did she bring you back? Was there a breakthrough in the dimensional technology? Who was with her on the call?
But your gaze slips, just for an instant, to the space beside her—to the black triangle suspended there, a strange little doll swaying from its form—and the question that finally escapes you is:

steps.speaker: Lemma
steps.content: <size=50>DON'T SAY IT!!!</size>
